name: Panteón de la Memoria, Cementerio de San Rafael, Málaga
story: After Málaga fell in February 1937, military courts and summary shootings killed thousands of Republican supporters, many against the wall of the old San Rafael cemetery. Their bodies were thrown into mass graves there. Between 2006 and 2009 archaeologists exhumed 2,840 bodies — one of the largest Civil War grave excavations in Spain. The cemetery has since been turned into a park and the remains placed in a memorial pantheon, inaugurated on 11 January 2014. Málaga had also seen heavy repression in the Republican zone in the first months of the war, before the city fell; the two waves of killing should be understood together.
see: A park on the site of the former cemetery with the Panteón de la Memoria, a monument holding the recovered remains, and walls of victims' names.
plan: Camino de San Rafael, in the Carretera de Cádiz district west of the centre; open during park hours, free.

boxes.text: Total victims of the Nationalist repression in Málaga are variously estimated at around 4,000 or more; killings in the Republican zone in Málaga (July 1936–Feb 1937) are estimated at around 2,500. Figures vary by historian.
